title: Data types
summary: Tell strings, numbers, booleans, null and undefined apart and check them with typeof.

docs.title: MDN: JavaScript data types and data structures

quiz.explain: `typeof` returns the type name as text. Anything in quotes is a string.

quiz.q: What is the type of the value 42.5?
quiz.explain: JavaScript has one number type for both whole numbers and decimals, so `typeof 42.5` and `typeof 42` are both `'number'`.
A variable declared without a value holds `undefined`, which means "nothing has been put here yet".

quiz.q: Which of these are booleans? Pick all that apply.
quiz.explain: Only `true` and `false` without quotes are booleans. `'false'` in quotes is a string and `0` is a number.
This is a famous historical mistake in JavaScript: `typeof null` is `'object'`. To detect null, compare with `value === null`.

exercise.task:
In `types.js`, write and export a function `typeName(value)` that returns the type of `value` as text:

- Normally the same text as `typeof value` (`'number'`, `'string'`, `'boolean'`, `'undefined'`).
- For `null` it must return `'null'` (not `'object'`).
hints: `typeof value` gives the answer for almost everything. `null` is the one special case.
Use an `if` statement to check `value === null` first and return `'null'`. Otherwise return `typeof value`.
